question: In the IMNCI young-infant algorithm, jaundice visible on the palms and soles of an 8-day-old baby is classified as a severe disease requiring urgent referral (Pink classification), even if the infant appears otherwise well and is feeding adequately.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and represents a critical IMNCI rule. Jaundice on the palms and soles signals bilirubin at a level associated with kernicterus risk. IMNCI mandates Pink (urgent referral) classification — adequate feeding does NOT downgrade this finding.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Jaundice extending to the palms and soles indicates severe neonatal jaundice — this is a Pink classification with mandatory urgent referral under IMNCI, regardless of feeding status or alertness. The clinical pearl reinforces: 'Jaundice on palms and soles = Pink, no exceptions.'
